react_result.final_narrative_text: The metabolomics profiling across control and treatment groups identified a striking enrichment of steroid hormone metabolites, with five C19/C18 steroids (dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, dihydrotestosterone, estrone, and 17β-estradiol) acting as the primary drivers of differential abundance. Over-representation analysis via RaMP-DB returned 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (KEGG:map00150 / SMPDB:SMP00068) as the top hit with an FDR of 2.9e-15 and a fold-enrichment of 1667, capturing 5 of 7 input steroids against 27 pathway members. MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirmed the same biological domain at the KEGG human namespace level (hsa00140, p = 2.5e-06), and mummichog m/z-direct activity scored 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' as its top-ranked pathway (p = 8.4e-05) with a remarkable 11/11 empirical-compound overlap, indicating near-complete pathway activation. Guanidoacetic acid and N-acetylgalactosamine were the two non-steroid hits; the former maps to glycine/serine metabolism and the urea cycle (MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism), while the latter resolves to N-acetylhexosamine metabolism (sialic acid, hyaluronan, keratan sulfate pathways), each significant only at the individual-compound level. The convergent steroid signal across ORA (RaMP, MetaboAnalystR) and m/z-network (mummichog) paradigms is biologically coherent: the androgen arm (DHEA → androstenedione → testosterone → DHT) and the estrogen arm (testosterone/androstenedione → estrone → estradiol via aromatase / CYP19A1) were simultaneously perturbed, suggesting either aromatase inhibition, altered 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase activity, or global disruption of steroid sulfotransferase/sulfatase cycling. This pattern is consistent with endocrine-active treatment exposure, steroidogenic tissue dysfunction, or hormone-responsive disease progression. The N-acetylgalactosamine hit may reflect altered glycosylation secondary to steroid-driven epithelial remodeling.
